translations.text: And he shall declare to him the sin that he has committed.

And for what he has sinned he shall offer to God a female from the flock, a lamb, or a kid from the goats, as a sin offering. And the priest shall make atonement for that sin, and the sin shall be forgiven him.
If he cannot afford a sheep, then for the sin he has committed he shall offer to God two turtledoves or two young pigeons: one as a sin offering and one as a whole burnt offering.
And he shall bring them to the priest, and the priest shall offer the one for the sin offering first. The priest shall wring its head off at the neck [?], but shall not divide it in two.
And he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the wall of the altar, and the rest of the blood he shall drain out at the base of the altar, for it is a sin offering.
And the second he shall make a whole burnt offering, as is required. And the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and it shall be forgiven him.

If he cannot find a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, then as his offering for his sin he shall bring a tenth of a measure of fine flour as a sin offering. He shall not pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.
And he shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take a full handful of it as its memorial portion and lay it on the altar of sacrifices before God. It is a sin offering.

And the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he committed in any one of these things, whichever he could find and offered, and it shall be forgiven him. The remainder shall belong to the priest, like a sacrifice of praise.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:

If a person forgets something through forgetfulness and sins unintentionally in regard to the holy things of God, then for his sin he shall offer to God an unblemished ram from the flock, valued in silver by weight, by the holy shekel, for the thing in which he became guilty.

And because he has sinned in regard to his holy things, he shall pay it back and add a fifth to it, and give it to the priest. And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and it shall be forgiven him.
And if a person sins and does any one of the things forbidden by the commandments of God, which ought not to be done, and did not realize it, and became guilty and incurred the sin,

he shall bring to the priest an unblemished ram from the flock, valued in silver, for his guilt. And the priest shall make atonement for his ignorance, in which he did not realize it and did not know, and it shall be forgiven him,
for he has committed a sin before God.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
If a person sins and heedlessly disregards the commandments of the Lord, and lies to his neighbor about a deposit, or about a partnership, or about robbery, or wrongs his neighbor in any way,
or if he has found something lost and lied about it, and sworn falsely about any one of these things that a person does and sins by them,
then when he has sinned and become guilty, he shall give back what he took by robbery, or make good the harm he did, or return the deposit that was entrusted to him, or the lost thing that he found,
or anything about which he swore falsely. He shall pay back the principal itself and add a fifth to it. He shall give it to the person to whom it belongs, on the day he is convicted.
And for his guilt he shall offer to God an unblemished ram, at the value of the thing in which he became guilty.
